title: xy + yz + zx = N (Borwein–Choi): a symmetric ternary problem solved up to one possible exception (none under GRH)
connection: Borwein–Choi determine the N not of the form xy + yz + zx (x, y, z ≥ 1) — 18 known exceptions plus at most one more unconditionally, the extra one excluded under GRH — via class numbers of Q(√−N). For an ES solution, xy + yz + zx = 4xyz/n (the pretzel determinant).
why: The same symmetric quadratic in x, y, z appears in ES; their class-number method (representations ↔ forms of discriminant −4N) is a proved-twin technique for a closely related equation.

title: Catalog: n = p + 2^k (de Polignac / Romanoff / Erdős)
connection: n = p + 2^k (de Polignac / Romanoff / Erdős) ↔ ES as a small-count existence problem. Expected witnesses/n: ≍ Σ_k 1/log n ≍ O(1) (log n terms each 1/log n). Obstruction: covering congruences {0 mod 2, 0 mod 3, 1 mod 4, 3 mod 8, 7 mod 12, 23 mod 24} force n−2^k divisible by a small prime. Status: false infinitely often (an AP of odd failures, Erdős 1950); Romanoff: positive lower density of representables. Mechanism: failure = periodic orbit k ↦ 2^k mod m covered by finitely many moduli; density = Romanoff's L¹ bound on r(n).
why: Canonical O(1)-count failure; ES has no periodic witness parameter, so the covering mechanism has no direct ES analogue — the reason why should be stated as a lemma.

title: Spinor exceptions as the analogue of T1
connection: Ternary forms fail to represent certain integers t·m² (spinor exceptional square classes) despite local solubility; ES Type I/II fails at odd squares m² despite local solubility (T1).
why: Both are square-class obstructions in a local-global problem; the spinor-exception theory (Schulze-Pillot, Earnest–Hsia) has a precise algebraic explanation that might map to T1.
first_step: Compute whether T1's failure set {m²} coincides with a spinor exceptional square class for some ternary lattice naturally attached to ES.
alt_first_steps: [dividing-0036] Look up whether a 'spinor norm' type invariant can be attached to the ES variety restricted to n = m².
[dividing-0252] Search for a half-integral weight form attached to ES counts (theta-type).
[signature-0150] Partition ES's failed subfamily by square-free part and check whether the missing primes align with a fixed spinor-exception square class.
[translate-0125] Test whether T1's empty square classes coincide with spinor-exceptional square classes of a ternary form attached to certificates (Λ_{d,m} Gross lattice) for small d,m.
[upgrades-0036] Compute spinor-exceptional classes for ternary forms of small discriminant; look for one whose exceptions are {m²} and whose representations of p biject with Type II data.

title: Bhargava–Hanke 290 theorem: finite test set
connection: Universality of a quadratic form is decided by finitely many small represented integers, matching F01 and a finite certificate/candidate reduction (F32); ES's finite congruence cover (F03) is a related finite reduction, though not a fixed test set.
why: It suggests searching for a finite arithmetic certificate that forces all inputs, rather than relying on a large computational range.
first_step: Read the 290 theorem proof's escalation and local-global steps; test whether ES's finite Mordell covering can be turned into an escalation criterion for certificate classes.
alt_first_steps: [dividing-0037] Ask whether there is an ES 'escalation' statement: if all primes up to B have certificates of some shape then all do? (likely false; record why).
[signature-0035] Ask whether 'the set of ES word-forms tuv−u−v with t in a finite set' has an escalation theory (which finite t-sets give all large primes?).
[tools-0162] Define ES escalation: start from a failing n, adjoin the identity family that covers it, iterate; check whether the escalation tree is finite for Mordell classes up to 10^9.
refs: Bhargava–Hanke, Universal quadratic forms and the 290-Theorem (preprint)
Rouse, Quadratic forms representing all odd positive integers, Amer. J. Math. 136 (2014)
